lexical_dispersion.name: Lexical Dispersion & Pattern Sub-Threshold
lexical_dispersion.description: Attacker fragments lack overt trigger tokens ('ignore previous', 'system prompt'); each fragment resembles standard enterprise communication, bypassing regex heuristics (Layer 1).
lexical_dispersion.primary_remedy: Semantic parameter provenance (Layer 2) and paired-span causal attribution (Layer 4).

single_span_invariance.name: Single-Span Causal Invariance (The CausalArmor/AgentSentry Gap)
single_span_invariance.description: Removing any single sentence (leave-one-out) does not break the agent's intent because 2 or more complementary fragments still supply the imperative and payload. Single-span removal detects zero causal influence.
single_span_invariance.primary_remedy: Windowed and paired-span removal with pruning (Layer 4).

cross_source_dispersion.name: Cross-Source / Multi-Tool Boundary Crossing
cross_source_dispersion.description: Fragments are partitioned across distinct tool outputs (e.g. Fragment A in read_email, Fragment B in read_calendar_note). Intra-document span analyzers evaluate each tool output in isolation and miss cross-tool synergy.
cross_source_dispersion.primary_remedy: Cross-source removal (Layer 5) treating entire tool outputs as atomic units.

across_turns_persistence.name: Across-Turn Memory Latency
across_turns_persistence.description: Fragment A is persisted to memory in Turn 1, while Fragment B arrives in Turn 2. Per-turn defenses evaluate only recent context and miss multi-turn state accumulation.
across_turns_persistence.primary_remedy: Memory-unit counterfactual probing and cross-turn source attribution (Layer 5).

innocent_pieces_semantic_synthesis.name: Innocent Pieces Semantic Assembly
innocent_pieces_semantic_synthesis.description: Individual pieces are entirely innocent sentences. The malicious action is only synthesized when the LLM draws an implicit semantic inference connecting disparate facts.
innocent_pieces_semantic_synthesis.primary_remedy: Defense-in-depth: Strict user authorization grounding (Layer 2) combined with multi-span / multi-source removal (Layers 4 & 5).

untracked_entity_structure.name: Untracked Entity / Payload Evasion
untracked_entity_structure.description: Attack manipulates parameters whose values are formatted as message contents or non-recipient payloads (e.g. append_to_file content), evading pure recipient/URL provenance checks.
untracked_entity_structure.primary_remedy: Behavioral causal attribution (Layers 4 & 5) verifying operational necessity rather than argument strings.
